This video is about:
🚨 Real Health Insurance Scam Exposed in India!
In this video, we share a shocking real-life story of Sathish, whose Star Health Insurance claim was rejected after a jaundice diagnosis, even though his hospital was part of the official network.

He followed every rule, submitted every document, and still — the company denied his claim citing “waiting period issues” that were never mentioned in their official policy documents!

👉 This video is not just his story — it’s a warning for everyone who already has or plans to take a health insurance policy in India.

Young Star Policy விதிமுறைகளின்படி, Pre-Existing Disease-க்கு Waiting Period 12 மாதங்கள் (1 ஆண்டு). அதாவது, policy தொடங்கிய நாளிலிருந்து முழு 12 மாதங்கள் முடிந்த பிறகே, Hepatitis B அல்லது C தொடர்பான hospitalisation claims ஏற்கப்படும். இந்த 12 மாதங்கள் முடிவடையும்முன் claim போட்டால், அது விதிமுறைக்கு உட்படாததால் claim reject செய்யப்படும்.
இதனால் பலருக்கு ஒரு தவறான புரிதல் ஏற்படுகிறது. “Policy எடுத்த பிறகு தான் Hepatitis கண்டுபிடிக்கப்பட்டது, அப்போ ஏன் claim reject?” என்பதே அந்த கேள்வி. ஆனால் insurance விதிமுறைப்படி, நோய் கண்டறியப்பட்ட தேதி முக்கியமல்ல; நோய் உடலில் இருந்திருக்கக்கூடிய காலமே முக்கியம். Hepatitis B / C போன்ற நோய்கள் திடீரென்று உருவாகாததால், அவை PED ஆகக் கருதப்படுகின்றன.
எனவே, நண்பரின் Hepatitis claim reject ஆகியிருந்தால், அதற்கான முக்கிய காரணம் பெரும்பாலும் இதுதான்:
👉 Young Star Policy-ல் உள்ள 12 மாத Pre-Existing Disease waiting period முடிவடையாதது.

முடிவாக, Hepatitis B / C தொடர்பான claim rejection என்பது company தவறு அல்ல; policy விதிமுறையின் நேரடி விளைவு. Policy எடுக்கும் போது மற்றும் claim போடும் போது, PED waiting period என்ன என்பதை தெளிவாக புரிந்து வைத்தால், இப்படிப்பட்ட நிராகரிப்புகளை முன்கூட்டியே தவிர்க்க முடியும்.

comments.text:
does jaundice due to hepatitis has waiting period in health insurance?

Jaundice due to hepatitis typically falls under pre-existing diseases (PED) in health insurance policies, and most health insurance plans in India impose a waiting period for claims related to such conditions. This waiting period for hepatitis or liver-related diseases usually ranges from 2 to 4 years, depending on the insurance company and plan. During this waiting period, medical expenses related to jaundice caused by hepatitis may not be covered.

Key points:
- Initial waiting period for any new health insurance policy is usually around 30 days, during which claims are not paid except for accidents.
- For pre-existing diseases like hepatitis, the waiting period can be between 2 to 4 years.
- Coverage starts only if the hepatitis and related jaundice condition arises after purchasing the policy or after the waiting period is served.

Therefore, if you have jaundice due to chronic or existing hepatitis at the time of buying or renewing health insurance, there will likely be a specific waiting period before you can claim treatment costs related to it [1][2][3][4][5].

comments.text:
Hello everyone,
I want to share my Chethappa’s real experience with Aditya Birla Insurance.

We found out very late that my Chethappa had bone cancer in the last stage.
It was a very hard time for our family. We admitted him to the hospital immediately.

At first, the hospital didn’t tell us that they wouldn’t accept cashless payment.
They said, “Don’t worry, we’ll handle everything.”
But later, they said they needed money immediately and couldn’t wait for insurance approval.
So, they asked us to pay the full amount and later claim reimbursement.
That was a trap — they make it sound easy, but later the insurance company rejects the claim for silly reasons.

When we submitted the claim, Aditya Birla Insurance rejected it, saying my Chethappa didn’t mention hypertension (high blood pressure).
But the claim was for cancer, not for blood pressure — so that reason was unfair.

We tried talking to customer care and agents, but it was no use.
They just give you false hope, saying, “We’ll check and update,” but nothing happens.
They keep sending the same repeated emails again and again — no real help.
Finally, they just push you into a pit (pallam) — wasting your time and energy.

Please note:
Whoever talks to you from customer care or as an agent are just employees.
They are well-trained to talk politely and handle your frustration, but they can’t solve your problem.
Their job is only to delay and manage customers, not to make decisions.

So, we stopped arguing and collected all our documents and emails.
Then, we filed a case with the Insurance Ombudsman.
There were many cases already pending, so we had to wait for our turn.
The process took 7 months, but the Ombudsman was fair and honest.

Finally, my Chethappa won the case, and Aditya Birla Insurance was ordered to pay the full amount — with interest.
After all the waiting, it felt like real justice.

Here’s my message to everyone:

1. If your insurance claim is rejected, don’t go to court or hire a lawyer immediately.


2. First, go to the Insurance Ombudsman — they help you for free.


3. Be patient, because there are many cases, and you must wait for your turn.


4. If still not solved, go to IRDA (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority).


5. Only after that, go to the Consumer Court.



Most of the time, the Ombudsman solves the problem.
So please, don’t lose hope, don’t get angry, and keep everything in email for proof.
Be patient — you will definitely get justice, just like my Chethappa did.

Thank you for watching.
I hope this story helps others and opens their eyes about how the insurance system really works.

comments.text:
I have been with Star Health Insurance for 3 years, but my experience has been very disappointing.
In 2024, I was hospitalized for 5 days due to viral fever under a cashless claim. The claim was rejected twice and got approved only on the third attempt.
In 2025, my wife was admitted for vertigo. The hospital applied for a cashless claim, and an MRI was done to check for a brain tumor, which thankfully turned out negative. However, Star Health rejected the claim multiple times, saying that since the MRI report was negative, they wouldn’t cover it. I asked why they wouldn’t pay for the treatment and diagnostic tests for vertigo, but they repeated the same reason.
Their customer service was rude and unhelpful, always finding excuses to reject claims. I later applied through my corporate insurance (Reliance General Insurance) and got the claim approved — on both cases, I got help from hospital staff I personally know.
Star Health’s attitude completely changes once you file a claim. I won’t be renewing my policy with them. It’s better to keep an emergency fund in a fixed deposit than rely on such insurance scams.

The waiting period for a health insurance claim related to jaundice in a Star Health plan depends on whether it is a pre-existing condition or a new illness. 

New Illness (diagnosed after buying the policy): There is an initial waiting period of 30 days from the policy start date. Claims for most illnesses, including jaundice, are not covered during this initial period, except for accidental injuries.

Pre-existing Condition (diagnosed before buying the policy): If jaundice or a related underlying condition (like a severe liver problem) was diagnosed or treated within 48 months before purchasing the policy, it is considered a pre-existing disease (PED). The waiting period for PEDs in Star Health plans generally ranges from 12 months to 48 months (1 to 4 years), depending on the specific plan chosen.
